subject: SEM in Lavaan : max number variables and data type

messages.author: ff9f865ae22ae237
messages.subject: SEM in Lavaan : max number variables and data type
parts:
Hi everyone,

I have developed a path model with one dependent variable, and different observed and latent variables.

To investigate my research question, I will use the method of Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), with the software of Lavaan in R, as I need to test if the variables in my path model (=theoretical model) are correlated, and thus if the causality of the model is supported by the sample data.

I have 2 questions :

- First, in my path model, I have 5 latent variables (constructed by different indicators) and 3 measures variables. In my theoretical model, I assume there are multiple direct and indirect effects between all these variables. Now, I was wondering, maybe I have too much variables ? and this will make it too complex ? is there a maximum of variables recommended ?
- Then, I was thinking of using polychoric correlation matrix as data input as the response data for all my latent variables are ordinal (data from an established questionnaire) but I also have my measured variables which are nominal data. Which type of data matrix do I use if I have a combination of ordinal and nominal data (=all categorical type of variables) ?

thank you for your help :)

kind regards,

Myriam

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: SEM in Lavaan : max number variables and data type
parts: - First, in my path model, I have 5 latent variables (constructed by different indicators) and 3 measures variables. In my theoretical model, I assume there are multiple direct and indirect effects between all these variables. Now, I was wondering, maybe I have too much variables ? and this will make it too complex ? is there a maximum of variables recommended ?
That involves a complex interaction between the sample size, reliability of indicators, and number of model parameters.

- Then, I was thinking of using polychoric correlation matrix as data input as the response data for all my latent variables are ordinal (data from an established questionnaire) but I also have my measured variables which are nominal data. Which type of data matrix do I use if I have a combination of ordinal and nominal data (=all categorical type of variables) ?

Nominal variables can only be exogenous in lavaan, and binary/ordinal variables should be declared as such, in order to analyze polychorics.

https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
